neet_che_u04_t07_1.working: When liquid water freezes to ice, its molecules become more ordered, so the entropy of the system decreases. Melting, evaporation and dissolution all increase disorder.

neet_che_u04_t07_2.working: ΔS_fus = ΔH_fus/T = 6000 J/mol ÷ 273 K ≈ 22.0 J K^-1 mol^-1. The value is positive because fusion absorbs heat.

neet_che_u04_t07_3.working: For isothermal expansion, ΔS = nR ln(V2/V1) = 8.314 × ln 10 = 8.314 × 2.303 ≈ 19.15 J/K. It is positive because the gas expands.

neet_che_u04_t07_4.working: A (free expansion): ΔS_sys = nR ln(V2/V1) and ΔS_surr = 0, so III. B (reversible adiabatic): isentropic, so I. C (phase change at boiling point): ΔS = ΔH/T, so IV. D (spontaneous process): ΔS_univ > 0, so II.

neet_che_u04_t07_5.working: A is false; not every exothermic process is spontaneous. B is true; melting of ice above 273 K is entropy-driven. C is true; at equilibrium ΔS_univ = 0. D is false; since ΔS = q/T, a given heat gives a smaller entropy increase at higher T. E is true; entropy is a state function. Correct set: B, C, E.
